zoroaster.summary: Prophet of Zoroastrianism, who framed existence as a moral contest between truth and falsehood — a dualism that shaped later Jewish, Christian and Islamic thought.
zoroaster.note: One of the widest genuine disputes in chronology. Linguistic analysis of the Gathas suggests roughly 1500–1000 BCE; Greek and later Zoroastrian sources suggest the seventh or sixth century BCE. The bracket spans both.

texts.title: Zoroastrian texts at the Internet Sacred Text Archive

iron-age.summary: Iron smelting spread across Eurasia and Africa, cheapening tools and weapons and reshaping the societies that adopted it.

kingdom-of-kush.summary: Nubian kingdom on the upper Nile that ruled Egypt outright as its 25th dynasty, and outlasted it by nearly a thousand years from Meroë, where it wrote in its own still only partly deciphered script.
